title: Ad Hoc Custom Credential Encryption Comparison
pattern: Verifying credentials or cryptographic signatures using simple direct string comparison operators (e.g. `==` in Rust or `strcmp` in C++).
why_bad: Direct string comparisons execute byte-by-byte and terminate on the first mismatched byte, creating timing side-channels. An attacker can measure request duration differences to determine the hash bytes sequentially, eventually reconstructing the correct credential.
detection: Standard string equality operations (`==`, `eq`, `strcmp`) used to validate password hashes, private keys, or signatures.
fix: Always perform security-sensitive credentials validation comparisons using constant-time comparison libraries that verify the entire array length regardless of mismatch position.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 5, p. 78.
